subject: ACME POC: Integration plan, success criteria & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acme.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Recap & Proposed POC Plan — Redwood + ACME

Thanks again for the demo today — great conversation. Quick recap and a proposed POC plan so we can align on success criteria, ownership, and timing. Please review and confirm or call out changes.

High-level goals (from today's discovery)
- Improve customer support summarization throughput and reduce query latency (target: 95th percentile < 250ms)
- Maintain classification/intent accuracy within 3% of current baseline
- Keep ongoing inference cost < $0.50 per 1k tokens (POC cost target)
- No persistent customer data stored outside ACME; sandbox data only for evaluation

Proposed POC (4 weeks)
1) Week 0 (this week): provisioning — provide sandbox keys, sample dataset, and SSO access for logs/metrics
2) Week 1: integration — SDK + API integration; streaming responses for conversational flows; function/tool-calling for action triggers
3) Week 2: eval run — run evaluation prompts/traffic, collect latency & quality metrics
4) Week 3: tuning & retest — batching/quantization suggestions, final metrics

Success criteria (proposed)
- Latency: 95th < 250ms under target load (TBD load profile)
- Quality: fall within 3% of current baseline on labeled eval set
- Reliability: <1% error rate, no auth failures
- Security: keys scoped to sandbox; logs retained per ACME policy

Technical notes / integration ask
- SDK: we recommend using our official SDK (npm: @redwood/inference) for token management and streaming helpers
- API routes: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate for sync; SSE/websocket available at https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate/stream for streaming tokens
- Embeddings: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings for vector workflows
- Function/tool calling: supported — send functions schema in the request, response includes structured call payload
- Suggested model for POC: redwood-1.3 (quantized variant available for cost reduction)

Owners / next steps
- ACME: Samantha (product lead) — confirm success criteria & provide sample dataset
- ACME: Tom (engineering) — will own integration work on their side
- Redwood: Marissa (AE) — program owner / commercial point
- Redwood: Dylan (SE) & Michael (platform) — technical leads for sandbox & integration

Attachments: ACME-POC-MAP.xlsx (baseline, sample data inventory)

If this looks good I'll ask Dylan and Michael to draft the technical runbook and get sandbox keys provisioned. Can you confirm owners and the 4-week cadence?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-18T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Recap & Proposed POC Plan — Redwood + ACME

High-level integration plan (technical) — I'll build the repo and short README. Summary below so we can hit the Friday target.

Step 0 — Provision
- Michael: create scoped sandbox API key (ACME-POC-001) with daily quota limits and telemetry forwarding to our staging metrics.

Step 1 — SDK install & auth (client/server) - npm: npm install @redwood/inference
- Example (Node):
  const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
  const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });

Step 2 — Sync generate (simple) - POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
- Body: {"model":"redwood-1.3","input":"..."}

Step 3 — Streaming (SSE) - Endpoint: https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate/stream - Example: open EventSource to the stream endpoint with the sandbox key; stream sends incremental token events and a final event with usage metadata.
- We will provide a minimal client snippet in the repo and a browser example for SSE handling.

Step 4 — Function / tool calling
- Send function definitions in the request JSON; the model will return a structured call when appropriate.
- We'll include an example for ticket creation: functions: [{name: "create_ticket", parameters: {...}}]

Step 5 — Embeddings & rerank (if they want)
- POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings with text payloads; return vectors for local similarity search.

Performance & config recommendations
- Batching: enable 50ms batching window or target batch size 8 for mid-load
- KV/prefix caching: recommend prefix cache for repeated context items (session keys)
- Quantization: use q4_0 variant for cost-sensitive flows

Rate limits & concurrency
- Default sandbox: 60 requests/min with 10 concurrent streams. We can increase if they need more for the POC — Michael can bump quotas per request.

Deliverables (this week)
- Repo: github.com/redwood/poc-acme (initial commit by EOD Thursday)
- Short README with code snippets for generate, stream, embeddings, and function-calling (I will add streaming example and error handling notes)
- Michael: sandbox key + SOC2 summary + redwood-poc-checklist.pdf attached

Let me know if you'd like me to include a sample server-side aggregator for latency metrics (we can provide a Grafana dashboard).

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-poc-checklist.pdf
